name: det-random-lua
title: Determinism S1 (B4, B6): seedable deterministic random and seedable Lua hash seed / math.random (issue #157)
issue: Analysis: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/physx-limitations-and-determinism.md (read sections 3, 4.4 and 5 fully first: the blocker inventory B1-B10 with file/line evidence; the line numbers are from master 7222391, re-verify each against the code before editing; docs/prose must be verified against CODE). This is stage 'S1 (cheap)' of the determinism plan (issue #157): small, CI-verifiable changes that are useful even without netcode (reproducible replays and tests). HARD RULES: default behaviour of every existing project/scene/test must be UNCHANGED unless the new setting/option is switched on; no protocol change; no network presets yet (that is stage S2, not this item); no new third-party dependency. Nothing builds locally; the PR's CI (9 checks) is the test, so write tests that run on every leg and keep platform-specific expectations out of them. List unverified items honestly. No Co-Authored-By trailer and no 'Generated with Claude Code' footer. SCOPE: (B6) add Math::DeterministicRandom (reuse the ParticleRandom integer-only algorithm: seedable, per-stream, no std distributions, no libm in its integer paths; for a unit-circle sample use an engine-side deterministic method or document that it is not libm-free); add an explicit seed API to the existing Random (e.g. Random.Seed(n) in Lua + C++) that, when called, switches Random.* to the deterministic generator; with no seed call behaviour is EXACTLY as today (random_device). (B4) Lua: `luai_makeseed` and the math.random seed currently come from time(NULL)/addresses (lstate.c:71-79, lmathlib.c:628-661, our build of external/lua): make both controllable from a project/engine setting `determinism.luaSeed` (unset = today's behaviour: randomised hash seed, time-seeded math.random; set = constant hash seed and math.random seeded from it). Think through and document the security note: a constant hash seed makes hash-flooding of string-keyed Lua tables possible, so it must stay OFF by default and the editor host must not enable it implicitly. Tests: same seed gives identical Random.* sequences and identical math.random sequences across two LuaRuntime instances in one process; pairs() order over a string-keyed table is identical across two states when the seed is set (and the test does not assert anything about the unset case). Docs: describe the setting and the 'no pairs() over gameplay state unless seeded' guidance. NOTE: sec-lua-budget (#159) is now MERGED: build on it: the Lua runtime now has LuaRuntime::RunChunk, LuaBudgetScope, the sandbox prelude (xpcall wrapper) and LuaPanicRepair; set the seeds where the state is created, without touching the budget/panic machinery; run the existing LuaBudgetTest suite unchanged. Also note the determinism hazard class found by #161: C++ does not fix function-argument evaluation order, so in any code or test you write, never call a stateful function (random, counter) more than once inside one argument list or operator expression.
acceptance: With no seed call/setting, behaviour is unchanged
Seeded Random and math.random sequences reproduce across two Lua states
Lua hash seed constant only when the setting is set; security note documented
Docs describe the API and the setting
notes: Reviewer: default path untouched, how luai_makeseed is overridden in our vendored Lua build is sound (compile definition vs patched file: is the local patch recorded in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES like the sol2 patches?), the seed is read before the first lua_State, tests do not depend on platform libm.
